intro:
BARNABY BARGAIN! My potions cure
exhaustion, doubt, and having money!

A demonstration battle is free.
The demonstration is mandatory.
defeat: A refund? On a free demonstration?
post:
My potion is water with confidence.
The confidence is locally sourced.

I am revising the label.
Apparently confidence needs testing.

intro:
VESPER VALE, phantom thief.
I have stolen your attention!

Please keep watching. My escape
plan depends on applause.
post:
I only steal discarded trinkets.
Mostly bottle caps.

The calling cards cost more than
the entire criminal enterprise.

intro:
MARLO MIRTH presents: a battle
with a completely impartial judge!

The judge is me in a different hat.
post:
I awarded myself second place.
You may have first.

There were only two contestants,
but I still made the podium.

intro:
SIR CLATTER! Rule one: no running!
Rule two: no reading rule one!

Rule three: battle the official
who has misplaced his whistle!
defeat: I appeal to a higher helmet!
post:
I wrote these rules to help people.
Then I ran out of useful rules.

Tomorrow: fewer rules.
That one is compulsory.

intro:
MOSSWICK! Behold my smoke bomb!
...That is a perfectly normal spore.

Quick! A battle before anyone
notices my grand entrance failed!
defeat: My grand exit is also a sneeze!
post:
My mushrooms refuse to prank anyone.
They have formed an ethics panel.

I am the only member under review.

intro:
I'm NYXIE. This parasol is for
maintaining an air of mystery.

It also keeps ash out of my hair.
Let us duel with practical elegance.
post:
I like quiet places. Not because
I'm tragic. They're simply quiet.

People keep offering me tissues
when I just want a bench.

intro:
SABLE. I started a protest against
being told to keep off the grass.

Then the grass asked us to move.
Battle me while we reconsider.
defeat: The grass has a strong argument.
post:
Being loud is easy. Listening
without planning your next shout?

That's the part I'm practicing.
Don't tell the band.

intro:
OPALINE. Yes, black lace and pink
ribbons can be on the same team.

My POKEMON settled the argument
by eating both fashion magazines.
post:
I design outfits for shy trainers.
One pocket is for emergency courage.

It's usually full of biscuits.
Courage travels surprisingly well.

intro:
CINDER. Mechanic. That buzzing
is my diagnostic equipment.

If it starts singing, duck.
Let's test the battle function first.
post:
I repair old machines because
someone once cared enough to build them.

Also, new machines have far fewer
interesting things wrong with them.

intro:
DAHLIA NOCT. These flowers are
not wilting. They're brooding.

A little battle should improve
their circulation and their reviews.
post:
People buy cheerful flowers for
sad friends. Sometimes a dark bloom
is the first honest thing in the room.

I still include care instructions.
Honesty also needs watering.

intro:
ECHO. Arcade champion. My strategy
is flawless if this is turn one.

After that, I call it an exciting
new difficulty setting.
post:
I used to reset every losing game.
Then I never learned the last level.

I'm keeping this loss.
It has useful information in it.

intro:
BRIAR. My jacket has thorns.
My team has thorns.

My sandwich was a logistical error.
Let's battle before lunch.
post:
I plant flowers in forgotten places.
The council calls it unauthorized.

The COMBEE call it lunch.
I value both forms of feedback.

intro:
FABLE. I'm collecting stories.
Every good one needs a challenge.

You look like a reasonable middle
chapter. Shall we begin?
post:
I leave the endings of my stories
blank until I meet the people again.

People deserve a chance to surprise
the person writing about them.

intro:
TAFFY! My team is adorable!
Also extensively trained!

Please admire the ribbons before
experiencing the consequences.
post:
Cute isn't the opposite of strong.
My JIGGLYPUFF can lift my suitcase.

Getting it to pack sensibly remains
a much more difficult operation.

intro:
ROUX. Bass player. Nobody notices
you until you stop playing.

My team would like to demonstrate
being very difficult to ignore.
post:
I used to play louder when I felt
left out. Now I ask for a solo.

It works better.
The neighbors wrote to thank me.

intro:
HUGO BOULDER. Our lunch committee
has reached a difficult question.

Is soup a beverage? We have agreed
to settle nothing and battle instead.
post:
OTIS says soup needs a spoon.
BASTIAN says the ocean disagrees.

I study stars. None of them
have volunteered to chair this meeting.

intro:
OTIS CRUMB. Baker, treasurer,
and keeper of the emergency biscuits.

This battle is not an emergency.
The biscuits disagree.
post:
The six of us split the bill evenly.
ORSON writes a poem on the receipt.

The waiter has asked us to stop
claiming poetry as legal tender.

intro:
BASTIAN TIDE. Marine botanist.
I asked whether the salad was local.

They showed me the kitchen.
Let's battle while I refine the question.
post:
I brought seaweed for the committee.
FLORIAN arranged it in a vase.

It does look lovely.
It also tastes considerably less lovely.

intro:
MONTY MALLOW. Skater. Our meeting
minutes contain no actual minutes.

I timed them. Forty-seven seconds.
We have plenty of room for a battle.
defeat: A new personal best at losing!
post:
I proposed wheels on the table.
HUGO proposed thinking first.

For the sake of the soup,
we have reached a compromise: chairs.

intro:
FLORIAN BLOOM. I've arranged the
flowers in order of battle readiness.

The centerpiece is undefeated.
I would like to catch up.
post:
We meet because six people can
make a bad week feel much smaller.

Also, OTIS brings bread.
We are allowed two reasons.

intro:
ORSON VELVET! I have composed
a sonnet to this humble sandwich.

It has fourteen lines and mustard.
Your battle shall be its final stanza!
post:
The others let me read my poems.
I let them finish lunch first.

Art needs an audience.
An audience needs a sandwich.

intro:
KESTREL. Weather courier.
Today's forecast: scattered challenges.

One is approaching from directly
in front of you. Battle now!
post:
I deliver weather reports by hand.
If I arrive soaked, I am also
the supporting evidence.

Nobody tips for that part.

intro:
JUNIPER. Climber. Three points
of contact at all times!

Unless you're throwing a BALL.
Then the lecture becomes a battle.
post:
I used to climb to prove I wasn't
afraid. I was afraid the whole time.

Now I check the ropes and climb
because I like the view.

intro:
SOLACE. I make wind chimes.
Each one has a different voice.

My team would like to test the
acoustics of a friendly battle.
post:
My first chime was made from
broken cups after we moved house.

I wanted something familiar to make
a sound in a place that wasn't yet.

intro:
IDRIS. Sky watcher. I have named
that cloud after my greatest rival.

It keeps changing shape to avoid
the rematch. You seem more reliable.
defeat: The cloud will be unbearable now.
post:
I chart the sky for travelers who
can't see the stars from their rooms.

Some nights all I can send is:
cloudy, but still up there.

intro:
FEN. Cartographer. This map says
the path is perfectly smooth.

My chair and I have filed a detailed
objection. Battle while the ink dries?
defeat: I'll mark that as a tough route!
post:
A good map tells you more than
where the stairs are. It tells you
which way you can actually go.

Mine includes benches, ramps,
and the best places to watch birds.

intro:
TARO. Tailor. I can repair a cape
while its owner is still posing.

My team calls that multitasking.
Let's add a battle to the schedule.
defeat: That strategy needs a new lining.
post:
Every patch on my coat came from
someone who taught me something.

This elbow was a lesson in
not sewing while wearing the coat.

intro:
COSMO! Master of the night sky!
Assistant manager of this afternoon!

For my next trick, a constellation
made entirely of POKEMON battles!
defeat: The stars request a brief interval.
post:
I learned the constellations wrong
and spent years calling one 'the sock.'

Children remember it better that way.
The sock is staying.

intro:
NETTLE. Tea connoisseur.
This cup needs three more minutes.

You look like a two-minute battle.
Do try to surprise me.
defeat: I'll put the kettle on again.
post:
People ask for the secret to a long
life. I tell them: let the tea cool.

It's not the whole secret,
but it prevents a very silly ending.

intro:
MIRI. Accordion player. I know
twelve songs and thirty apologies.

My team knows a battle arrangement.
Please hold your applause until we stop.
defeat: That was the extended apology mix.
post:
I play requests for sailors.
Mostly songs that remind them of home.

I pretend not to notice when they
sing the wrong words very carefully.

intro:
ZEPHYR. Street dancer. That stumble
was part of the routine.

So is this battle.
Please don't ask about the next stumble.
defeat: A daring return to floor level!
post:
I teach dance to people who say
they have two left feet.

My SPINDA has four directions
and none of them are right. We manage.

intro:
ELDEN GLIMMER. Photographer.
I've waited an hour for perfect light.

My team has decided to manufacture
some. A battle should do it.
post:
I used to chase rare photographs.
Now I return to the same small pond.

Something changes every evening.
You have to stay long enough to notice.
